title: Adding Ruffles
content: **List of Contents** Importing File Drafting the Ruffle Patterns Sewing the Ruffles to the Dress Arranging Patterns using Superimpose Sewing the Side Seams Simulation **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-g_Adding%20Ruffles.zip) for Adding Ruffles** **Importing File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hMGWfThp6o \- Open the file, Dress_Ruffle, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then g_Adding Ruffles. Double click on the file, Dress_Ruffle, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Drafting the Ruffle Patterns** * **Drafting the Front Ruffle YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tCBlUsZaVIk **\- Select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024292928/mceclip0.png) **Rectangle** tool from the 2D Toolbar to draft the front ruffle. Click and drag on the 2D grid and create a rectangular Pattern that is longer than the front hem edge. * **Creating the Back Ruffle YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=87OV4K72dpY **\- **Copy** and **Paste** the front ruffle Pattern to create the back ruffle. \- Select the **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Right click on the front ruffle Pattern in the 2D Window. Select **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)** from the pop-up menu. \- A ghost of the copied Pattern will follow the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D grid to Paste. **Sewing the Ruffles to the Dress** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MV4bGOS2akQ \- Use the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024293208/mceclip2.png) **Segment Sewing** tool to sew the ruffles to their respective dress hemlines. **Arranging Patterns using Superimpose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C-_4xT5gzNY \- Use **Superimpose** to easily arrange Patterns based on their Sewing Lines. \- Using the**![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024210227/mceclip3.png) Select/Move** tool, select the ruffle Patterns in the 3D Window. They will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. Right click either of the ruffles to access the pop-up menu. Select **Superimpose(Side)** to set the ruffles at the sweep of the dress. **Sewing the Side Seams** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RCsBto1hlUQ \- Use the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024293208/mceclip2.png) tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew the side seams of the ruffles together. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tbGdkNXdjDs \- Click on the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) Simulate icon in the 3D Toolbar to drape. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Constructing a Fly and Zipper Closure
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window Sewing Patterns Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window Sewing the Fly Shut Simulation Adding Buttons and Buttonholes **[Download exercise file](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360098477913/Pants_Fly.ZPrj) for Adding Ribbing** **Opening a Project File** \- Open the file, Pants_Fly, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then f_Constructing a Fly and Zipper Closure. Double click on the file, Pants_Fly, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mc7e-dKA1JM \- Duplicate the fly Pattern. \- Since the fly Patterns will not be Symmetrized, duplicate it via Copy and Paste. \- To do so, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. In the 2D Window, click on the fly Pattern. Hold down Ctrl or Cmd +C to Copy the Pattern. Then, hold down Ctrl or Cmd +V to Paste. A ghost of the copied Pattern will follow the mouse cursor until it is placed. Click on 2D grid to place the Pattern. Take care not to overlap Patterns. **Sewing Patterns** * **Sewing The Fly to the Pants YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7-HQFT0KaVU **\- There are two Patterns for the fly: one will be sewn to the wearer’s right pant front and the other will be sewn to the wearer’s left pant front. \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024289608/mceclip3.png) **Free Sewing** tool to sew one part of the fly to the Center Front seam of the wearer’s left pant leg Pattern. To avoid accidentally easing the fly into the Center Front seam, create the first Sewing Line on the fly Pattern. This way, when a Sewing Line is started on the Center Front of the wearer’s left pant leg, a blue dot the exact length of the fly will appear on the pant Pattern outline. \- The second part of the fly will be sewn under the wearer’s right pant leg Pattern. Using the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024206367/mceclip2.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar, select the purple Baselines on the wearer’s right pant leg Pattern and hit the Enter key on the keyboard to generate the Internal Lines. Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024289608/mceclip3.png) **Free Sewing** tool to sew the fly to the wearer’s right pant leg Pattern. * **Changing Sewing Line Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yQ6P-LzJuzc **\- The second part of the fly is sewn under the wearer’s right pant leg Pattern, completely overlapped. If overlapping Patterns are sewn with **Flat** Sewing Lines, there is a higher chance of collision and Simulation instability when they are folded together. To prevent this, change **Flat** Sewing Lines to **Turned** Sewing Lines within the Property Editor. \- Use the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026656887/mceclip0.png) Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to select the Sewing Lines that join the fly Pattern and the left pant leg Pattern. Navigate to the Property Editor and change the **Sewing Line Type** to **Turned**. The fly will lay flat when Simulation is activated. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window** * **Arranging the Fly on the Right Pant Leg Pattern YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zT4j4anKBw **\- The fly needs to be arranged under the wearer’s right pant leg Pattern. \- Navigate to the 3D Toolbar and select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png)****Select/Move** tool. Right click on the fly Pattern that is sewn to the wearer’s right pant leg to access a pop-up menu. Choose **Superimpose (Under)** to arrange half of the fly underneath the wearer’s right pant leg Pattern. * **Arranging the Fly on the Left Pant Leg Pattern YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fC5Q193oRDo **\- If the Avatar is obstructing Pattern visibility, hide the Avatar. Navigate to the Vertical View Toggle Menu and hover over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png)****Avatar Display** —the second icon of the Vertical View Toggle Menu—to view a horizontal row of icons. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024207067/mceclip10.png) **Show Avatar**. \- The remaining fly Pattern needs to be arranged. Place it at the Center Front of the wearer’s left pant leg Pattern. \- To do so, navigate to the 3D Toolbar and select the Select/Move tool. In the 3D Window, click on the fly to access the Gizmo tool. Use the Gizmo tool to arrange the Pattern properly. Make sure to place this half of the fly behind the previously arranged fly Pattern on the left. \- Click on ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024207067/mceclip10.png) **Show Avatar** to view the Avatar again. **Sewing the Fly Shut** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y7rXPrHwNLo \- The Center Fronts of the fly Patterns will be sewn together, acting as a zipper closure. \- Select the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024206367/mceclip2.png)**Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the purple Baselines marked on the Center Fronts of the fly Patterns. They will be Traced as Internal Lines. \- Use the ![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024207107/mceclip11.png) **Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew the newly created Internal Lines on the fly Patterns together. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DceNqkTdMzM \- Turn on ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** in the 3D Toolbar to drape. **Adding Buttons and Buttonholes** * **Adding a Buttonhole YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RgZl1XiMU9M **\- Add a Buttonhole to the overlap of the waistband. \- Select the ![mceclip12.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024289988/mceclip12.png) **Buttonhole** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window. The waistband Pattern is marked by purple Chalk Lines to indicate the Buttonhole placement. Click once on the Pattern to add a Buttonhole. A line, representing the Buttonhole, will appear on the 2D Pattern and an image of the Buttonhole will appear in the 3D. * **Adding a Button YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dEw8awHpO3U **\- Add a Button to the underlap of the waistband. \- Select the ![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024207147/mceclip13.png) **Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window. The waistband Pattern is marked by purple Chalk Lines to indicate the Button placement. Click once on the Pattern to add a Button. A circle with a cross in the middle, representing the Button, will appear on the 2D Pattern and a Button will appear in the 3D. * **Fastening Button and Buttonhole YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UcrroV7l3tM **\- Select the ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024290008/mceclip14.png) **Fasten Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click on Button and Buttonhole to pair them up in either in the 2D or 3D Window. The selection order does not affect Simulation. \- The Button will appear on top of the Buttonhole it is paired with. The lock icon hovering above the pair indicates that the Button and Buttonhole has been fastened. \- To adjust the **Bind Position** of Buttons, select the Buttonhole with the ![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024290048/mceclip15.png) **Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. Navigate to **Bind Position** in the Property Editor. Click and drag the slider to adjust the value Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive tutorial for creating and assembling a fly zipper closure on pants using CLO software, including step-by-step instructions and video resources for each process.

title: Adding Ribbing
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Establishing Sewing Lines Arranging Patterns Folding the Ribbing Freezing Patterns Simulation Sewing the Side Seams of Ribbing Patterns Particle Distance Final Simulation **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-e_Adding%20Ribbing.zip) for Adding Ribbing** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nS8ShlWgGiY \- Open the file, T-Shirt_rib, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then e_Adding Ribbing. Double click on the file, T-Shirt_rib, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Establishing Sewing Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mUdWYgYXdJ8 \- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Sew the sleeve Patterns and the ribbing together. **Arranging Patterns** * **Using Arrangement Points ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=whpPBYkMOJ0 \- Navigate to the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D Window. Hover the mouse over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png)****Avatar Display** icon and a horizontal row of icons will appear. Select **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)****Show Arrangement Points**. \- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png)****Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar. Click on the ribbing Patterns and place them on the Arrangement Points on the Avatar’s wrists. * **The Arrangement Submenu ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AFYaLSYgdX0 \- Currently, the Arranged ribbing Patterns overlap themselves. This can lead to unstable Simulation. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and scroll down to the **Arrangement** submenu. Adjust **Offset** to modify the overlap. To move the ribbing slightly closer to the ground, lower the **Position Y** value. **Folding the Ribbing** \- To avoid deformation of the 3D Garment, fold the ribbing prior to Simulation. * **Drawing a Fold Line ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fuckp6SX1oo \- The **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png)Fold Arrangement** tool can only be applied to seamlines and Internal Lines. \- Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the**![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024287748/mceclip4.png) Internal Polygon/Line** tool. Using the midpoints on the sides of the ribbing Patterns, draw a fold line. \- Navigate to the 3D Window. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png)****Fold Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click on the newly created fold line and the Fold Arrangement Gizmo tool will appear. If parts of the Fold Arrangement Gizmo tool are difficult to access, rotate around the Avatar until the tool is fully visible. Use the arrows to fold the ribbing in half. Repeat for the other side. * **Assigning a Fold Angle ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9bmIqpt5jkk \- To fold ribbing more precisely, assign a **Fold Angle** to the fold lines. \- Select the fold lines on the 2D Patterns with the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191348/mceclip7.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Navigate to the Property Editor. Under **Fold** , set the **Fold Angle** to **0** degrees. * **Establishing Sewing Lines ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hh9XYcAAm_U \- The folded ribbing Patterns need to be sewn. \- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Sew the upper half of the ribbing to its lower half. **Freezing Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tXVRSiwyFzA \- Freeze all the Patterns except the ribbing to maintain the current drape of the 3D Garment. \- With the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205047/mceclip6.png) **Transform Pattern** tool selected, click and drag over all the Patterns in the 2D grid. Make sure to encompass all the Patterns within the marquee box to select them. Selected Patterns will be highlighted in yellow. Hold down the Shift key from the keyboard and deselect the ribbing Patterns. \- Navigate to the 3D Window. Right click on one of the selected Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Select **Freeze**. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZVY9tBc1wnE \- Click on the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205067/mceclip7.png)Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to drape. When the Patterns are folded correctly, turn off **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205067/mceclip7.png)Simulate**. **Sewing the Side Seams of Ribbing Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZD6EpiYFic0 \- Using the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool, sew the side seams of the ribbing Patterns together. \- Turn on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205067/mceclip7.png)Simulate**. When the ribbed Patterns are fully draped, turn off **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205067/mceclip7.png)Simulate**. **Particle Distance** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V5lyU-Evxlg \- Lower the **Particle Distance** of the ribbing for better Simulation. \- Select the ribbing Patterns in either the 3D or the 2D Window and navigate to the Property Editor. Scroll down to the **Simulation Property** submenu and decrease the **Particle Distance** value to **5**. **Final Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wWHWc3B_jro \- **Activate** the Frozen Patterns. \- With the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205047/mceclip6.png) **Transform Pattern** tool selected, click and drag over all the Patterns in the 2D grid. Make sure to encompass all the Patterns within the marquee box to select them. Navigate to the 3D Window and right click on one of the selected Patterns. A pop-up menu will appear. Select ACTIVATE. \- Turn on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024205067/mceclip7.png)Simulate** to apply the changes. \- The ribbing will drape alongside the other parts of the 3D Garment more naturally. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for adding ribbing to garments in CLO, providing step-by-step instructions and video resources for each stage of the process.

title: Adding Elastic to Express Smocking
content: **List of Contents** Importing File Adding Elastic to Create Smocking Unfreezing Patterns Simulation Fabrics Particle Distance Changing the Avatar Pose **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-c_Adding%20Smocking.zip) for Adding Elastic to Express Smocking** **Importing File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SYbCglU23do \- Open the file, Dress_Smocking, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then c_Adding Smocking. Double click on the file, Dress_Smocking, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. \- Note that the bodice Patterns of this particular file are Frozen, indicated by their ice blue color. ** Adding Elastic to Create Smocking** \- Use ELASTIC to Express Smocking. * **Tracing Smocking Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vy3yM9Pekl0 \- Trace the purple Baselines as Internal Lines. \- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024166087/mceclip0.png)Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar and click on the purple Baselines where ELASTIC will be applied. Select multiple Baselines by holding down the Shift key while clicking. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete Tracing. * **Applying Elastic** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J4wpwHQpJXo \- Select the Internal Lines that **Elastic** will be applied to. To select multiple Internal Lines conveniently, **Lock All Patterns**. Navigate to the 2D Window and right click anywhere on the 2D grid to access a pop-up menu. Select **Lock All Patterns**. Then, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Navigate to and click on the 2D grid next to the bodice Patterns. Drag across all the Internal Lines created within the bodice Patterns. The marquee box should fully encompass all the Internal Lines to select them properly. \- In the Property Editor, check the checkbox next to **Elastic** to activate the function. A few options, such as **Strength** and **Ratio** , will appear below **Elastic**. Adjust the **Ratio** to **50**. \- In addition to the Internal Lines, **Elastic** needs to be applied to both the top and bottom Pattern outlines of the front and back Patterns. Unlock the bodice Patterns. Right click anywhere on the 2D grid to access a pop-up menu. Reselect **Lock All Patterns** to unlock previously locked Patterns. \- Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191348/mceclip7.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. Select the top and bottom Pattern outlines of both the front and back bodice Patterns. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard while selecting to select multiple segments. The selected Pattern outlines will be highlighted in yellow. Navigate to the Property Editor and check the checkbox next to **Elastic** to activate the function. A few options, such as **Strength** and **Ratio** , will appear below **Elastic**. Adjust the**Ratio** to **50**. \- Both the Internal Lines and the Pattern outlines where **Elastic** has been applied will shorten by 50% of their original length. **Unfreezing Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k46qiR39FBY \- **Unfreeze** the bodice Patterns before Simulating. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool in the 2D Toolbar. In the 2D grid, click and drag over the bodice Patterns to select them. The marquee box should fully encompass all the bodice Patterns to select them properly. Right click on one of the selected bodice Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Select **Unfreeze** and the Patterns will return to their original colors and textures. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CIlM-q-ZIhQ \- Click on the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024248448/mceclip2.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to drape. The bodice will tighten around the Avatar. \- The smocking details lack realism due to two things: a stiff Fabric and a large **Particle Distance**. **Fabrics ** * **Creating Chiffon** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OWWermczvc0 \- Click the +Add icon to add a new Fabric to the Fabric list within the Object Browser. Select the newly added Fabric to adjust its properties. \- In the Property Editor, scroll down to the option Physical Property. Click on the drop down arrow next to Preset and select **R_Chiffon**. As Chiffon is very malleable and lightweight, the shirring will appear more detailed than if the garment was created out of a thicker fabric such as Denim. * **Applying the Fabric onto the 3D Garment** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gOAh3TRcVjI \- Activate ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024248448/mceclip2.png) **Simulate** to see the drape change in real-time. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. In the 2D grid, click and drag the mouse over all of the Patterns so that they are fully encompassed within the marquee box. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate that they have been selected. \- Navigate to the Object Browser. Assign Chiffon to all of the Patterns by clicking on the Assign to Selected Patterns icon next to the Chiffon Fabric. The changes are reflected immediately on the 3D Garment. **Particle Distance** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uXAw0mxWGYY \- Decrease the **Particle Distance** value to attain a more realistic drape. \- Select the bodice Patterns in the 2D Window, navigate to the Property Editor and scroll down to Simulation Properties. Change the **Particle Distance** value to **5**. \- ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024248448/mceclip2.png) **Simulate** to apply the changes. \- While the garment is Simulating, use the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024168147/mceclip3.png) **Select/Move** tool to refine the smocking detail. \- Decrease the **Particle Distance** of the skirt Patterns to **5**. **Changing the Avatar Pose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JR5YBpsCMtg \- Change the Avatar Pose from A-pose to have her stand at attention. \- To apply the Pose, navigate to and double click on the default folder named Pose in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatar faces will appear—double click on the folder that matches the Avatar in the 3D Window. Double click on or drag and drop the file F_B_pose_02_attention.pos to apply the pose. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive tutorial for CLO 3D users, outlining the step-by-step process to import files, add elastic for smocking, simulate fabrics, and customize avatar poses.

title: Constructing a Vent
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Using the Fold Arrangement Tool to Fold a Vent Simulation Sewing a Vent **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-b_Constructing%20a%20Vent.zip) for Constructing a Vent** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LULfM3gMXJY \- Open the file Jacket_vent for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then b_Constructing a Vent. Double click on the file, Jacket_vent, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Using the Fold Arrangement Tool to Fold a Vent** * **Tracing a Fold Line ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yRqrkdJuqbM \- The **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png)Fold Arrangement** tool can only be applied to Seamlines and Internal Lines. Thus, Chalk Lines and Baselines must be Traced as Internal Lines in order to fold them. \- The fold lines are marked by purple Baselines on the Patterns. Select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024165347/mceclip0.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar and click on both Baselines to Trace them as a single Internal Line. \- With the Baselines selected, hit the Enter key to generate the Internal Line. \- Since the Patterns have been Symmetrized, the Baseline only needs to be Traced on one of the Patterns. Symmetrically Pasted Patterns mirror one another, so if one of the pair has an Internal Line added to it, the other will reflect this change. * **Folding a Vent ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ruVyHtpk7cA \- Hover the mouse over the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026655587/mceclip0.png) **3D Garment Display** icon (the first icon of the Vertical View Toggle Menu) and a horizontal row of icons will appear. Select**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026655647/mceclip3.png) Show Internal Lines** to display the Internal Lines on the garment. \- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png)****Fold Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click on the newly created fold line and the Fold Arrangement Gizmo tool will appear. If parts of the Fold Arrangement Gizmo tool are difficult to access, rotate around the Avatar until the tool is fully visible. Use the arrows to fold one side of the vent. Repeat for the other side. * **Assigning a Fold Angle ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xHySgfPGjqA \- To fold the vent more precisely, assign a FOLD ANGLE to the fold lines. \- Select the fold lines on the 2D Patterns with the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239368/mceclip4.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Navigate to the Property Editor. Under **Fold** , set the **Fold Angle** to **0** degrees. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dn_7CSHxrlQ \- Click on the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to drape. When the Patterns are folded correctly, turn off ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) **Simulate**. **Sewing a Vent** * **Establishing Sewing Lines ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NyNkLUf_rp8 \- Sew parts of the vent to refine its shape. \- Sew the top segments of the vent together. Then, sew the bottom of the vent on the wearer’s left to the wearer’s back left pattern of the jacket. Be mindful of Directional Notches. As the jacket back Patterns have been Symmetrically Pasted, the Sewing Lines established on the left side are reflected onto the right. * **Changing Sewing Line Type ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6jkCgeDpVyU \- There are two types of Sewing Lines: **Flat** and **Turned**. \- If overlapping Patterns are sewn with Flat Sewing Lines, there is a higher chance of collision and Simulation instability when they are folded together. To prevent this, change **Flat** Sewing Lines to **Turned** Sewing Lines within the Property Editor. \- To do this, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026693928/mceclip5.png) **Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on a Sewing Line and navigate to the Property Editor. Click the drop down arrow next to **Sewing Line Type**. Select **Turned** Sewing. \- The vent will now lay flat. * **Simulation ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1l2uI0j5roE \- Click on the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239708/mceclip7.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar briefly to reflect the newly added Sewing Lines. \- To hide the Internal Lines, navigate to and hover over the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026655587/mceclip0.png) **3D Garment Display** icon again. Select **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026655647/mceclip3.png)****Show Internal Lines** and the Internal Lines will no longer be visible on the 3D Garment. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Refining a Jacket: Sleeve Heads
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Adding Sleeve Heads **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/D_Fine_Tuning/D-a_Refining%20a%20Jacket%20Adding%20Shoulder%20Pads%20and%20Sleeve%20Heads.zip) for Refining a Jacket: Sleeve Heads / Adding Shoulder Pads** **Opening a Project File ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_XYL1Crcek4 \- Open the file, Refining a Jacket, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to D_Fine Tuning, then a_Refining a Jacket Adding Shoulder Pads and Sleeve Heads. Double click on the file, Refining a Jacket, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Adding Sleeve Heads** \- Sleeve heads are added to give shape and structure to sleeves. \- In this particular exercise, only one sleeve head will be added. * **Assigning the Width of the Sleeve Head YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TT9UBLqv13E **\- Measure the total length of the armhole before drafting the sleeve head Pattern. \- Use the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345768/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar to select all the Pattern outlines of the armhole. Navigate to the Property Editor and under Selected Line, there is an option called **2D Line Length**. This value is the total length of the selected Pattern outlines. * **Making the Sleeve Head Pattern YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nICtIG_eEiY **\- Select the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024261387/mceclip1.png) **Rectangle** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Navigate to the 2D Window and click anywhere on the 2D grid to access the Create Rectangle pop-up window. \- Enter the armhole length (previously measured under 2D Line Length) for the **Width** and **10mm** for the **Height**. * **Sewing the Sleeve Head YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=macXGJLUG5Q **\- Sew the sleeve head to the armhole. Use the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345848/mceclip4.png) ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345828/mceclip3.png) **M:N Sewing** tool to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024261567/mceclip5.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024261587/mceclip6.png) **Free Sewing** tool to select the respective ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345848/mceclip4.png) ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345828/mceclip3.png) **M:N Sewing** tool. * **Arranging the Sleeve Head in the 3D Window YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tIJGzzaQ1sI **\- Arrange the sleeve head in the 3D Window using **Superimpose (Under.)** \- To do so, using the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345888/mceclip7.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, select the sleeve head Pattern. Right click on the Pattern to access a pop-up menu. Select **Superimpose (Under)** to arrange the sleeve head underneath the sleeve Pattern. \- Make sure that the sleeve head is arranged below the sleeve Pattern and not the jacket body Patterns. * **Simulation YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jQqJgh3BuBc **\- Use the **Layer** function on the sleeve to mitigate Simulation instability between the overlapping sleeve head and sleeve Patterns. \- Using the **Transform Pattern** tool, select the sleeve Patterns in the 2D Window. In the 2D grid, click and drag over all the sleeve Patterns. Make sure that the marquee box fully encompasses the Pattern to select them properly. Then, navigate to the Property Editor, scroll down to **Layer** under Simulation Properties. Change the value to **1**. \- Activate ![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345908/mceclip8.png) **Simulate** until the sleeve Patterns are completely settled over the sleeve head. \- Reset the LAYER value to 0. * **Adjusting the Add'l Thickness - Collision of the Sleeve Head YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hhfDlgIhpNY **\- Increase the **Add'l Thickness - Collision** of the sleeve head Pattern to account for the thickness of the seam when the seam allowances of the sleeve and armhole are sewn together. \- To do so, select the sleeve head Pattern with the Transform Pattern tool from the 2D Toolbar. Navigate to the Property Editor and scroll down to **Add'l Thickness - Collision** under Simulation Property. Change the value to **4**. * **Particle Distance YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=47BJw_78ySU **\- Since the sleeve head Pattern is relatively thin, decrease the **Particle Distance** to **5** to mitigate Simulation instability. \- Using the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345888/mceclip7.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, select all the sleeve head Pattern. In the 2D grid, click and drag over the sleeve head Pattern. Make sure that the marquee box fully encompasses the Patterns to properly select them. Navigate to the Property Editor and scroll down to **Particle Distance** under Simulation Property. Change the value to **5**. * **Changing the Physical Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2EMxb_L31yI **\- Assign a rigid Fabric to the sleeve head. \- Using the **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, right click on the sleeve head Pattern to access a pop-up menu. Select **Assign to New Fabric**. A new Fabric will be added to the Object Browser—the new Fabric will also be applied to the selected sleeve head Pattern. \- Select the new Fabric from the Object Browser and navigate to the Property Editor. Scroll down to find Preset. Select **Trim-Fusible Rigid** from the drop-down menu. \- Activate ![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345908/mceclip8.png) **Simulation** to apply the changes. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive tutorial for refining a jacket by adding sleeve heads and shoulder pads, complete with instructional videos and downloadable exercise files.

title: Adding Padding
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Generating Design Lines for Padding Creating the Second Layer Adjusting Pressure Simulation **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-i_Adding%20Padding.zip) for Adding Padding** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=13D0Fqk8dUU \- Open the file, Jacket_Padding, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then i_Adding Padding. Double click on the file, Jacket_Padding, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Generating Design Lines for Padding** * **Adding Internal Lines to the Jacket Body** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s66x0yYlVZI \- Use **Offset as Internal Line** to generate Internal Lines to use as design lines for padding. \- Select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024343108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the hemlines of the front and back panels in the 2D Window. Right click on one of the selected lines. Select **Offset as Internal Line** from the pop-up menu. \- The **Offset as Internal Line** pop-up window will appear. Assign the number of Internal Lines to generate and their offset **Distance**. Click **OK** to create the Internal Lines. * **Adding Diagonal Internal Lines to the Sleeve Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kG68L_MhmDo \- Use the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024258887/mceclip1.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** tool from the 2D Toolbar to freehand a diagonal Internal Line on the Patterns in the 2D Window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024258907/mceclip2.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the diagonal Internal Line and Copy it by holding down the Ctrl or Cmd + C key on the keyboard. Press Ctrl or Cmd + V to Paste—a ghost of the copied Internal Line will follow the mouse. Hold down the Shift key and dashed orthogonal guidelines will appear in the 2D Window. Use them to figure out placement for the Internal Line, then right click on the Pattern. The Paste pop-up window will appear. \- Assign the number of Internal Lines to generate and their offset **Distance**. \- Click **OK** to create the Internal Lines. \- All the newly created Internal Lines will continue to be highlighted in yellow, indicating that they are still selected. Right click on one of the Internal Lines and a pop up menu will appear. \- Select **Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline**. * **Expressing Quilting with Internal Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-RqVXP4cOY \- Select all of the newly created Internal Lines on the sleeve Patterns to **Copy** and **Mirror Paste** them onto the Pattern. \- In order to avoid selecting the Pattern while selecting the Internal Lines, lock the Patterns. To do so, right click on the 2D grid and select **Lock All Patterns** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will appear greyed out to indicate they have been locked. \- With the **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar selected, click and drag over the sleeve Patterns, making sure all of the Internal Lines are within the marquee box. Copy the lines by pressing Ctrl or Cmd + C and Mirror Paste by pressing Ctrl or Cmd + R. A ghost of the copied Internal Lines will follow the mouse. Click on the Pattern to place them. \- Unlock the Patterns by right clicking on the 2D grid and select **Lock All Patterns** from the pop-up menu. **Creating the Second Layer** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I_eyoM8OpdE \- Padded garments consist of three layers: the shell, the wadding, and the lining. In CLO, **Pressure** acts as the wadding. The Patterns need to be copied, or cloned, with the **Layer Clone** function so that there is a shell layer and a lining layer. \- Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024258907/mceclip2.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, select all of the Patterns. Right click on one of the Patterns and select **Layer Clone (Over)** from the pop-up menu. This will place the Cloned Patterns on top of the original Patterns in the 3D Window, making them the outer shell layer. If details such as pockets have already been sewn on top of the original Patterns, select **Layer Clone (Under)** to place the Cloned Patterns underneath the original Patterns in the 3D space, making them the inner lining layer. \- A ghost of the Cloned Patterns will follow the mouse until they are placed. Click on the 2D grid once to place the Cloned Patterns, preferably so they do not overlap with the original Patterns in the 2D Window. \- **Pressure** will not be applied to the zippers, so a second layer of these Patterns is not needed. Select and delete the Cloned zipper Patterns. **Adjusting Pressure** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=36OhgMowR2k \- Adjust **Pressure** to inflate the 3D Garment. \- Distinguish which of the two layers is the outer shell and the inner lining of the 3D Garment. \- Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024258907/mceclip2.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, select all shell Patterns, navigate to the Property Editor, and scroll down to **Simulation Property**. **Pressure** is the last option in that submenu. Adjust the **Pressure** value to **20**. \- Repeat for the lining Patterns, but adjust their **Pressure** value to **-20**. \- Do not adjust **Pressure** values for the zipper Patterns. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qokjVBSOD2w \- Click on the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024345148/mceclip3.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to drape. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive tutorial for adding padding to garment designs in CLO, guiding users through the essential steps of opening project files, generating design lines, creating layers, and adjusting pressure simulations.

title: Adding Pleats - Box Pleats
content: **List of Contents** Loading an Avatar Importing a DXF File Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window Adding Box Pleats to the Skirt Sewing the Rest of the Garment Simulation With Strengthen Simulation With Unstrengthen Changing the Avatar Pose Hiding the Internal Lines **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-h_Adding%20Pleats.zip) for Adding Pleats - Knife Pleats / Box Pleats** **Loading an Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iPva1tM83Ho \- This tutorial will cover how to make a skirt with box pleats. \- This is a Women’s skirt. Load a female Avatar from the Library. \- Navigate to and double click on the default folder named Avatar in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatars will appear—double click on or drag and drop either female Avatar into the 3D Window. ** Importing a DXF File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kSnCboq1euM \- Import the file, Box_Pleats.dxf, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then h_Adding Pleats. Double click on the file, Box_Pleats.dxf, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. \- If the practice folder has not been added to the Library, navigate to File > Import > **DXF (ASTM/AAMA)**. Locate the file, Box_Pleats.dxf, and click Open to import the file. Set the units to mm and then click OK to finish importing the skirt. **Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window** * **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)**** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EuPnlkhOqtI \- Only half of the Skirt Patterns have been provided. Duplicate the front and back Patterns as Symmetric Patterns to complete the 3D Garment. Use the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024218607/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar to select the Patterns. In the 2D grid, click and drag the mouse over all the Patterns so that they are fully encompassed within the marquee box. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. \- Right click on one of the Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Navigate to the section labeled **Clone Patterns with Linked Editing**. Select **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)**. \- A ghost of the copied Patterns will follow the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D grid to Paste. Both the selected Patterns and any Sewing relationships they have will be duplicated. * **Arranging the Cloned Patterns in the 2D Window ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RliPAlLXACM \- Place the duplicated Patterns near the original Patterns. Using the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024218607/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, move the duplicated back Pattern close to the original back Pattern in the 2D Window. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window** * **Syncing Pattern Arrangement ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PJocWQ-mYt4 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026680027/mceclip0.png) **Reset 2D Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar to reflect the Pattern layout in the 3D Window as it is in the 2D Window. * **Arranging Patterns on Arrangement Points ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qILjqFtIsc \- Turn on the Arrangement Points. \- In this particular exercise, the Patterns have been Symmetrized and all the Arrangement Points are linked. Therefore, arranging half of the skirt Patterns on the Avatar will automatically arrange the other half of the skirt similarly on the other side. \- All Arrangement Points, except for those that are placed around the torso of the Avatar, are linked in CLO ver4.0.0. Symmetrized Arrangement Points have light-blue outlines around them. **Adding Box Pleats to the Skirt** * **Creating Fold Lines ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dmiEYz3qWEE \- In order to fold pleats, the Pattern needs to have fold lines. Use the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024302288/mceclip1.png) **Trace** tool to generate Internal Lines that will serve as the fold lines. Select the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024302288/mceclip1.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the purple Baselines that will be converted into Internal Lines and hit the Enter key on the keyboard. * **Assigning Fold Angles Using the Pleats Fold Tool ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spqmUyTelr4 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026717088/mceclip0.png) **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Set the direction the pleats’ fullness will be folded towards. To do so, click a point on the skirt Pattern after the first Internal Line and move the mouse—an arrow will follow the cursor, indicating the direction that the pleats will be folded. Making sure the arrow crosses over the entire skirt Pattern but stopping right before the last Internal Line, double click to finish setting the direction. When the **Pleats Fold** pop-up window appears, select **Box Pleats** and click **OK**. * **Sewing the Pleats ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oVAiUwBYl_A \- Use the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024302348/mceclip4.png) **Free Sewing** tool to sew the Center Front and side seam sections of the skirt Patterns to the Center Front and side seam sections of the yoke Patterns. Make sure not to catch any parts of the Pattern that belong to the pleats. \- For the pleated portion of the skirt, use the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024214067/mceclip3.png) **Pleats Sewing** tool to establish Sewing Lines. Select the Pleats Sewing tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the part of the yoke Pattern that has not been sewn, the one closest to Center Front, and drag along the Pattern outline. Stop after reaching the Sewing Line near the side seam. This is the first half of the seam. For the second half of the seam, click on the starting point of the pleats on the skirt Pattern and drag along its Pattern outline. Click at the end of the pleats to complete the Sewing Line. \- Make sure the direction the Sewing Lines are being established in follow the direction that the pleats fullness will be folded towards. **Sewing the Rest of the Garment** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xMa5ZEwDM2E \- Sew the remaining Patterns, using either the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024218807/mceclip3.png) **Segment** or**![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024302348/mceclip4.png) Free Sewing tools**. \- Use the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024218867/mceclip6.png) ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024302368/mceclip5.png) **M:N Sewing** tool to attach the yoke Patterns to the waistband. **Simulation With Strengthen** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LExQXMnT5fI \- **Strengthen** adds a temporary stiffness to Patterns and helps create crisply folded pleats. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024218607/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool. Then, on the 2D grid, click and drag over all the Patterns. Ensure that all Patterns are fully encompassed within the marquee box. Right click on one and select **Strengthen** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will appear orange in the 3D Window to indicate they have been Strengthened. \- Activate ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024298088/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** and the pleats will fold sharply and precisely. **Simulation With Unstrengthen** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6Fqg80FIkM \- **Unstrengthen** the skirt Patterns when the pleats finish Simulating. To Unstrengthen the Patterns, select all of them, right click on one, and select **Unstrengthen** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will no longer appear orange in the 3D Window. \- Activate ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024298088/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** again to see the actual drape of the skirt. **Changing the Avatar Pose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kh9JSM6k2co \- Change the Avatar Pose from A-pose to have her stand at attention. \- To apply the Pose, navigate to and double click on the default folder named Pose in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatar faces will appear—double click on the folder that matches the Avatar in the 3D Window. Double click on or drag and drop the file pose_02_attention.pos to apply the pose. **Hiding the Internal Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GA6bO2EfQzw \- To hide the Internal Lines, navigate to and hover over the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024214727/mceclip7.png) **3D Garment Display** icon again. Select ![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024214747/mceclip8.png) **Show Internal Lines** and the Internal Lines will no longer be visible on the 3D Garment. Go back to the List of Contents
