Go to C_Details, then h_Adding Pleats. Double click on the file, Knife_Pleats.dxf, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. \- If the practice folder has not been added to the Library, navigate to File > Import > **DXF (ASTM/AAMA)**. Locate the file, Knife_Pleats.dxf, and click Open to import the file. \- Set the units to mm and select AUTO TRACE INTERNAL LINES. Then, click OK to finish importing the skirt. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window ** * **Arranging the Waistband Patterns With Arrangement Points ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yTDlqU580a4 \- Turn on the Arrangement Points. Hover over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png)****Avatar Display** icon—the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu—and click on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)****Show Arrangement Points** , which is the second icon in the horizontal Avatar Display series. Blue dots, the Arrangement Points, will appear on the Avatar in the 3D Window. \- Place the waistband Patterns on the Arrangement Points located at the front and backside of the Avatar’s waist. * **Arranging the Skirt Pattern With the Gizmo Tool ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pwkwQM4xBZ0 \- Because the skirt Pattern is very wide, the front and back skirt Patterns will overlap if they are arranged with Arrangement Points. There is a higher chance of collision and Simulation instability when large portions of Patterns overlap each other. To avoid this, use the **Gizmo** tool to place the front and back skirt Patterns around the Avatar. **Adding Knife Pleats to the Skirt** * **Assigning Fold Angles With the Pleats Fold Tool** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMGsBdFchsQ \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026717088/mceclip0.png) **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Set the direction the pleats fullness will be folded towards. To do so, click on the 2D grid next to the skirt Patterns and move the mouse—an arrow will follow the cursor, indicating the direction that the pleats will be folded. Making sure the arrow crosses over the entire skirt Pattern, double click to finish setting the direction. When the **Pleats Fold** pop-up window appears, select **Knife Pleats** and click **OK**. * **Sewing Pleats With the Pleats Sewing Tool** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zgl0s2Wl7yM \- Select the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024214067/mceclip3.png) **Pleats Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Start Sewing by clicking on one end of the waistband and click again once the mouse has reached the end of the Pattern. This is the first half of the seam. For the second half of the seam, click on the starting point of the skirt and click again once the mouse has reached the end of the Pattern to complete Sewing. \- Make sure the direction the Sewing Lines are being established in follow the direction that the pleats fullness will be folded towards. **Sewing the Side Seams of the Skirt** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UNlvfpBJrp0 \- Use the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024297768/mceclip4.png) **Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew the side seams of the skirt Patterns. Be mindful of the Directional Notches while sewing so as not to twist any Sewing Lines. **Simulation With Strengthen** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tYfRkpPDrnQ \- **Strengthen** adds a temporary stiffness to Patterns and helps create crisply folded pleats. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024297828/mceclip5.png) **Transform Pattern** tool. Click and drag over all the Patterns in the 2D grid. Ensure that all Patterns are fully encompassed within the marquee box. Right click on one, and select**Strengthen** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will appear orange in the 3D Window to indicate they have been Strengthened. \- Activate ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024298088/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** and the pleats will fold sharply and precisely. **Simulation With Unstrengthen** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fGcOMTM-ZDA \- **Unstrengthen** the skirt Patterns when the pleats finish Simulating. To Unstrengthen the Patterns, select all of them, right click on one, and select **Unstrengthen** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will no longer appear orange in the 3D Window. \- Activate ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024298088/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** again to see the actual drape of the skirt. **Changing the Avatar Pose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lLp9x1zrUOc \- Change the Avatar Pose from A-pose to have her stand at attention. \- To apply the Pose, navigate to and double click on the default folder named Pose in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatar faces will appear—double click on the folder that matches the Avatar in the 3D Window. Double click on or drag and drop the file pose_02_attention.pos to apply the pose. **Hiding the Internal Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=etFAuxia9xc \- To hide the Internal Lines, navigate to and hover over the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024214727/mceclip7.png) **3D Garment Display** icon again. Select ![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024214747/mceclip8.png) **Show Internal Lines** and the Internal Lines will no longer be visible on the 3D Garment. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive tutorial for creating a women's skirt with knife pleats in CLO 3D, providing step-by-step guidance on loading avatars, importing files, and simulating designs.

title: Constructing a Shirt Placket
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Cut & Sew Expressing a Shirt Placket Applying Bonding **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/C_Details/C-d_Constructing%20a%20Shirt%20Placket.zip) for Constructing a Shirt Placket** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IGIi65PVjI0 \- Open the file, Shirts_placket, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to C_Details, then d_Constructing a Shirt Placket. Double click on the file, Shirts_placket, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Cut& Sew** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wEwYRlfsgH8 \- Currently, the placket and the body Patterns are merged into a single Pattern. Use **Cut & Sew** to split the Pattern into two. \- Select the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024250468/mceclip1.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar and right click on the purple Baseline of the shirt front. A pop-up menu will appear. Select **Cut & Sew**. The shirt front Patterns will be split into two at the Cut Line (the Baseline that was selected initially). In addition, Sewing Lines will automatically be established between the placket Patterns and the shirt front body Patterns. **Expressing a Shirt Placket** * **Adjusting Add'l Thickness ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rQ0f9mHL2FM \- To express a placket’s actual thickness, as it is usually a multi-layered Pattern, adjust the **Add'l Thickness** value of the Patterns. Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024170107/mceclip2.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, select all the placket Patterns and navigate to the Property Editor. Scroll down to **Add'l Thickness - Rendering**. Enter **3mm**. \- To see the changes in the 3D Window, navigate to the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D Window and hover the mouse over the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026694488/mceclip0.png) **Textured Surface** icon – the third icon from the Vertical View Toggle Menu. A horizontal row of icons will appear. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026656567/mceclip1.png) **Thick Textured Surface**. The thickness of the Patterns are now reflected on the 3D Garment. * **Expressing Double Layers ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xmH23xGRTPs \- To express turned edges, round the Pattern edges. Select all the placket Patterns using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024170107/mceclip2.png) **Transform Pattern** tool in the 2D Window. Navigate to the Property Editor and check the option **Curved Side Geometry**. \- To express a single-layer placket as a double-layered one, check the **Double Sided** option on in the **Curved Side Geometry** submenu. The placket will no longer appear single-layered. **Applying Bonding** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dNwrTWA1PTE \- To express interfacing, select the placket Patterns and use the **Bond** function. \- Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024170107/mceclip2.png) Transform Pattern** tool. In the 2D grid, click and drag over all the placket Patterns. The Patterns must be fully encompassed within the marquee box to be properly selected. They will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and scroll down to **Bond/Skive**. Click the white arrow to expand the menu and check the checkbox next to **Bond**. The placket Patterns will change to a deep champagne color in both Windows to indicate that **Bond** has been applied. \- ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024248448/mceclip2.png) Simulate to apply the changes. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for constructing a shirt placket, including detailed instructions, video tutorials, and downloadable exercise files.

title: Check Fit
content: **List of Contents** Change Pose Fix Neckline and Armhole Length Draw Avatar Tape Align Shoulder Lines **Change Pose ** \- An Avatar with both arms open is used to easily drape Garments. When the 3D Garment is completed draped on an Avatar or a Dummy, apply the Attention pose to the Avatar to check fit. \- To change the Avatar’s pose, load the Pose file from the Pose folder in the Library window. Be careful to select the folder for the same Avatar currently in use to correctly load matching Avatar. Double click the Attention Pose file. **Fix Neckline and Armhole Length ** \- In the 3D window, you can check the 3D Garment’s neckline and armhole are stretched. To prevent the stretch of the neckline and the armhole due to the weight of the Garment, apply seam tapes around the neckline and armhole. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026895728/mceclip1.png) **Seam Taping** tool from the 2D toolbar and click the neckline and armhole to apply seam tapes. \- Once the **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png)****Simulation** is activated, you may check the neckline and armhole are no longer stretched. **Draw Avatar Tape ** \- To check fit accurately, the 3D Garment’s shoulder lines must match with the Avatar’s shoulder line. \- To see Avatar’s shoulder line clearly, use the Avatar Tape function to draw avatar tapes on the Avatar. Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026860807/mceclip2.png) **Linear Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D toolbar and hover the mouse over the Avatar. Then, click a start point and an end point to create an Avatar tape. \- To create an Avatar Tape around a part of the Avatar, use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026895748/mceclip3.png) **Circumference Avatar Tape** tool. When using this tool, to assign the start, directional, and end points, click three times. ※Note: Now Linear Measure avatar tape tools are grouped into 6 measure tools. The line drawn by "Linear Measure" can't do "Attach to Tape". "Tape Measure and Circumference Measure" is the correct tool to create the tape for attachment. (ver6.0) **Align Shoulder Lines ** \- Activate the **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png)****Simulate** tool and drag the 3D Garment to match its shoulder lines to the Avatar’s. \- Repeat the same procedure to match shoulder lines for both sides. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step guidance on adjusting garment fittings for avatars, including changing poses, fixing neckline and armhole lengths, drawing avatar tapes, and aligning shoulder lines.

title: Correcting Improper Sleeve Simulation
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Simulate Solution A – The Reset 3D Arrangement (All) tool Solution B – The Select Mesh tool **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/E_Fixes/E-f_Correcting%20Improper%20Sleeve%20Simulation.zip) for Correcting Improper Sleeve Simulation** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Q2XNyTUad8?rel=0 \- This tutorial will cover how to correct improper sleeve Simulation. \- Open the file, Correcting Improper Sleeve Simulation, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to E_Fixes, then f_Correcting Improper Sleeve Simulation. Double click on the file, Correcting Improper Sleeve Simulation, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Simulate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dUDYUSpWs-o?rel=0 \- The Patterns have already been arranged around the Avatar. \- Turn on ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317927/mceclip0.png) **Simulate**. The sleeves have Simulated incorrectly around the wrists. **Solution A – The Reset 3D Arrangement (All)** * **Checking 3D Arrangement** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zYk8jygH3n8?rel=0 \- Turn off ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317927/mceclip0.png) **Simulate**. Navigate to the 3D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024357608/mceclip0.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement (All)** tool. Patterns will return to their Arrangement prior to Simulation. Zoom in near the Avatar’s wrists and look at the Pattern placement. During Arrangement, if the sleeve Patterns do not encompass the Avatar’s wrists, they will drape outside of them. * **Tilting Sleeve Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pG3tTIsEEcg?rel=0 \- Change to a Front view by pressing 2 on the keyboard. Select the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024318387/mceclip1.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar. In the 3D Window, click on the wearer’s right sleeve Pattern to access the Gizmo tool. Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo tool and slightly tilt the Sleeve Pattern. Then, click on the yellow box of the Gizmo tool to push the sleeve Pattern back. Make sure that the sleeve Pattern completely surrounds the Avatar’s right wrist. Repeat for the wearer’s left sleeve. \- Rotate around the Avatar to check that all the Patterns have been Arranged correctly. * **Simulate ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YPBAXdFkFo8?rel=0 \- Turn on ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317927/mceclip0.png) **Simulate**. The sleeves should drape properly around the Avatar’s arms. **Solution B – The Select Mesh tool ** \- To practice Solution B, reopen the file, Correcting Improper Sleeve Simulation. Turn on Simulation to drape the garment on the Avatar. * **Making a Selection ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PepaeP2gQog?rel=0 \- Since only a portion of the sleeves are draped outside the Avatar’s wrists, use the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024318487/mceclip2.png) **Select Mesh** tool to solve the problem. \- Select the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024318487/mceclip2.png) **Select Mesh** tool from the 3D Toolbar and the Patterns’ mesh will be visible in green in both the 3D and 2D Windows. To make a precise selection, navigate to the 2D Window. Click on the 2D grid next to the Sleeve Pattern and drag over the section of the sleeve that draped incorrectly. The selected area will be highlighted in lime green. (To learn how to use the Select Mesh tool in detail, reference the Index, [Select Mesh](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012227007).) ** **\- Navigate to the 3D Window. Click on the lime green selection and move it so that it surrounds Avatar’s wrist. Repeat selecting and moving the mesh for the other sleeve. * **Simulate ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uJ8gQVCughQ?rel=0 \- Turn on ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317927/mceclip0.png) **Simulate**. The sleeves should drape properly around the Avatar’s arms. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide and tutorial videos for correcting improper sleeve simulation in CLO, featuring step-by-step solutions and downloadable exercise files.

title: Enhancing the Quality of a Garment
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Using the Hi-Res Garment Tool Simulation Using the Low-Res Garment Tool – Fine-Tuning or Fixing Any Deformation of the Garment Simulation Reapplying the Hi-Res Garment Tool **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/D_Fine_Tuning/D-d_Enhancing%20the%20Quality%20of%20a%20Garment.zip) for Enhancing the Quality of a Garment** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DRooiHFByHo \- This tutorial will cover how to enhance the quality of a garment. \- Open the file, Jacket_Enhancing the Quality, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to D_Fine Tuning, then d_Enhancing the Quality of a Garment. Double click on the file, Jacket_Enhancing the Quality, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Using the Hi-Res Garment Tool** * **Hi-Res Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kY8B8H258qo \- To enhance the quality of a garment, Particle Distance, Add'l Thickness - Collision, Skin Offset, and Simulation Quality must be adjusted. Use the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354328/mceclip1.png) **Hi-Res Garment** function to edit their values. \- Navigate to the 3D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354328/mceclip1.png) **Hi-Res Garment** tool. A pop-up window will appear with options for the Garment, Avatar, and Simulation, that can be adjusted. Click **OK** to apply the settings. \- To learn more about the**![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354328/mceclip1.png) Hi-Res Garment** tool, reference the index [Hi-Res Garment](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380608). * **The Default Setting ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aKEnwEOiyek \- The default setting of the Hi-Res Garment function is appropriate in most cases. \- The default setting is as follows:**Particle Distance = 5.0mm** , **Add'l Thickness - Collision = 1.0mm** , **Skin Offset = 0.0mm** , and **Simulation Quality = Complete.** * **Deselecting the Add'l Thickness - Collision ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b14y02fwzgM \- In cases where Patterns need to have different **Add'l Thickness - Collision** values, such as a garment with shoulder pads, uncheck the checkbox next to the **Add'l Thickness** option so that the value (1mm) is not applied to all of them. \- Shoulder pads have been included in this file. The 3D Garment and the shoulder pads will have different **Add'l Thickness - Collision** values. Uncheck the checkbox next to **Add'l Thickness - Collision**. Click **OK** to apply the changes. * **Simulation ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pkqqj5Utt8s \- Once the Hi-Res Garment tool has been applied and the**Simulation Quality** has been changed to **Complete** , the **Simulate** icon will change from a ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024270267/mceclip2.png) single arrow to a ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354428/mceclip3.png) **double arrow**. Turn on Simulation—the icon will glow orange to reflect the change as well. Simulation will take longer but drape more accurately. Turn off Simulation when the 3D Garment is fully Simulated. * **Adjusting the Add'l Thickness - Collision ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=byniT75jbgs \- To enhance the quality of the garment even further, adjust the **Add'l Thickness - Collision**. \- Select all the Patterns except the shoulder pad Patterns. Select the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024270447/mceclip4.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. In the 2D grid, click and drag over all the Patterns. Make sure the Patterns are fully encompassed within the marquee box. While holding down the Shift key, deselect the shoulder pad Patterns by clicking on them. Now that only the 3D Garment Patterns are selected, navigate to the Property Editor and change their **Add'l Thickness - Collision** value to **1**. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=udqwpLmBRDY - Activate ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354428/mceclip3.png) **Simulate** to apply changes and check for any deformation of the 3D Garment. **Using the Low-Res Garment Tool – Fine-Tuning or Fixing Any Deformation of the Garment ** \- For this section of the tutorial, open the file Dress_Enhancing the Quality. \- To do so, hover over the folder, d_Enhancing the Quality of a Garment, within the Library. Double click on the file, Dress_Enhancing the Quality, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. * **Low-Res Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sZijm-8taMY \- Occasionally, the garment may deform during Simulation. As previously mentioned, changing the **Simulation Quality** to **Complete** (via the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354328/mceclip1.png) **Hi-res Garment** function) slows down Simulation considerably. Making changes to the 3D Garment after applying this change is not recommended. \- Instead, lower the resolution of the garment to fix any issues that may have occurred during Simulation with the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354928/mceclip5.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool. \- Navigate to the 3D Toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354928/mceclip5.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool. A pop-up window will appear with options for the Garment, Avatar, and Simulation, that can be adjusted. Click **OK** to apply the settings. * **The Default Setting ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBbdXvIjZZU \- The default setting of the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354928/mceclip5.png) **Low-Res Garment** function is appropriate in most cases. \- The default setting is as follows: **Particle Distance = 20.0mm** , **Add'l Thickness - Collision = 2.5mm** , **Skin Offset = 3.0mm** , and **Simulation Quality = Normal.** * **Adjusting Particle Distance ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T85NnVNEGnQ \- If the difference between the **Particle Distance** values before and after enhancing the quality of the garment is too wide, the general drape of the 3D Garment can change dramatically. To avoid this, change the **Particle Distance** as needed. \- For this specific file, adjust the **Particle Distance** to **10**. **Simulation** \- Once the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354928/mceclip5.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool has been applied, the Simulate icon will revert from a ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354428/mceclip3.png) double arrow to a ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024270267/mceclip2.png) **single arrow**. * **Fine-tuning a Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SnEkNJDlFro \- For this particular exercise, fine-tune the portions around the Armholes. While ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024270267/mceclip2.png) **Simulate** is still activated, use the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024271127/mceclip6.png)**Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar to pull and straighten crumpled parts of the garment. * **Fixing Deformation of the Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XXj8CzdCCTM \- If the 3D Garment has Simulated improperly, fix the issues as needed. \- Reference the Fixes category to view the appropriate tutorials. **Reapplying the Hi-Res Garment Tool** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QlRBKv2TbPE \- Up the resolution of the 3D Garment by selecting the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024354328/mceclip1.png) tool from the 3D Toolbar. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024270267/mceclip2.png) **Simulate** once more. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive tutorial guide for enhancing the quality of garments using the Hi-Res and Low-Res Garment tools, complete with step-by-step instructions and video resources.

title: Aligning Shoulder Seams
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Aligning the Shoulder Seams Enhancing the Quality of the T-shirt Deleting Avatar Tape **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/D_Fine_Tuning/D-c_Aligning%20Shoulder%20Seams.zip) for Aligning Shoulder Seams** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dP3KIwU1dwc \- This tutorial will cover how to align the shoulder seams of the T-shirt and evaluate the fit. \- Open the file, T-Shirt_Aligning Shoulder Seams, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to D_Fine Tuning, then c_Aligning Shoulder Seams. Double click on the file, T-Shirt_Aligning Shoulder Seams, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Aligning the Shoulder Seams** * **Attaching the Shoulder Seams to Avatar Tape YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uHjWlvJiZ2c ** * **Establishing Avatar Tape on the Avatar** \- Press**5** on the keyboard to switch to a Top view. \- Select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024268507/mceclip0.png) **Linear Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D Toolbar. A blue Point will follow the mouse cursor. To start drawing the Avatar Tape, click once on the High Point Shoulder. Drag the mouse cursor towards the Shoulder Point, holding down the Shift key to create a straight line. Double click to complete the Avatar Tape. * **Attaching the Shoulder Seams** \- Use the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024352568/mceclip1.png) **Attach to Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D Toolbar. Click on the shoulder seam and the Patterns will turn transparent. Then, click on the previously established Avatar Tape. Both edges should appear red. * **Simulation** \- Click on the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024352748/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar and the shoulder seams will shift and attach to the Avatar Tape. \- Press **2** on the keyboard to switch to a Front view. Check and make sure the shoulder seams are attached to the Avatar Tape. * **Fine-tuning the T-shirt ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDF_eC69GMQ \- If the shoulder seams were sitting far away from the actual shoulder, the garment will move dramatically and may result in a messy drape. To resolve this, gently pull at the garment until it sits properly on the Avatar. **Enhancing the Quality of the T-shirt** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jjq5pACv2oU \- Select the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024268627/mceclip4.png) **Hi-Res Garment** tool from the 3D Toolbar, adjust the options as needed, and click OK to increase the resolution of the T-shirt. **Deleting Avatar Tape** * **Deleting Avatar Tape ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ygiKkT8iGwI \- Delete the Avatar Tape to smooth out the shoulder seams. \- After increasing the resolution of the T-shirt, delete the Avatar Tape using the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024352728/mceclip5.png) **Edit Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D Toolbar. To do so, rotate around the Avatar as needed to clearly see the Avatar Tape on the shoulders. Click on the Avatar Tape and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. * **Simulation ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dL9tAHYy6og \- Activate ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024352748/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** to apply the changes. Go to D_Fine Tuning, then b_Refining a Jacket Fine-Tuning the Shell. Double click on the file, Refining a Jacket, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Refining a Jacket** * **Particle Distance YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q-vvAWosTg8 **\- To enhance the quality of the Simulation, decrease the **Particle Distance** of the Patterns to **10** in the Property Editor. **Particle Distance** is located under the **Simulation Property** submenu. * **Simulate YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_tgsIjlfE4g **\- Click on the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024268007/mceclip1.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to apply the changes. * **Adjusting the Jacket YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fdwv-IhYuyg **\- The jacket is shifted towards the back. title: Correcting Improper Button Simulation
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Straightening the Placket Patterns Repositioning Buttons Simulation **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/E_Fixes/E-e_Correcting%20Improper%20Button%20Simulation.zip) for Correcting Improper Button Simulation** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qCSHpONYWCk \- The tutorial will cover how to correct improper Button Simulation. \- Open the file, Correcting Improper Button Simulation, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to E_Fixes, then e_Correcting Improper Button Simulation. Double click on the file, Correcting Improper Button Simulation, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Straightening the Placket Patterns** * **Re-simulating Placket Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AfXeSPU75NM \- The placket Patterns are twisted due to being improperly Arranged before Simulation. Select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317107/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar. Click on the right placket Pattern. Use the Gizmo tool to pull it forward away from the Avatar. \- Turn on ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024401788/mceclip2.png) **Simulate**. * **Straightening the Placket Patterns with the Pin tool ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PL6omqLO9KE \- Keep Simulation on. With the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317107/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool selected, hold down the W key and click on the 3D Garment, specifically the twisted portions of the placket Patterns, to add Pins. Release the W key to stop adding Pins. There are two ways to move Pins. The first is to click on a Pin—the Gizmo tool will appear. Use it to move Pins in space until the Patterns are straightened. The second method is to click and drag the Pin into place. Repeat the process as needed. The right placket Pattern should sit properly on top of the left placket Pattern. When the Patterns have been appropriately adjusted, right click on the 3D Garment to access a pop-up menu. Select **Delete All Pins**. **Repositioning Buttons** * **Checking Button Simulation ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LIsC959up4A \- When the placket Patterns are straightened, check to see if the Buttons Simulated correctly. \- Some of the Buttons are still hidden under the placket Patterns. * **Repositioning Buttons ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ExIaczaZ6B8 \- One way to fix incorrectly Simulated Buttons is to reset them. Select the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024193988/mceclip5.png) **Select/Move** **Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. Navigate to the 2D Window and select all the Buttons on the wearer’s left placket Pattern. To do so, click on the 2D grid next to the Pattern and drag so that all the Buttons are within the marquee box. The selected Buttons will be highlighted in yellow. Right click one of the selected Buttons to access a pop-up menu. Select **Reset 3D Position**. In the 3D Window, the Buttons will relocate to the top of the placket Patterns. \- The Gizmo tool can also be used to reposition hidden or rotated Buttons. * If a Button is still hidden under the placket, select it in the 3D Window using the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024317107/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar. The Gizmo tool will appear. Click and drag the blue axis forwards to pull the Button out of the placket. Use the yellow square to further adjust the Button’s position. * If a Button is rotated incorrectly or flipped, use the Gizmo tool to fix it. Click and drag the relevant rotational handle until the Button faces the front. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0d-_5omZlaM \- Turn on ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024401788/mceclip2.png) **Simulate**. The Buttons should sit nicely on the placket. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Simulation Instability-A Portion of the Garment
content: **List of Contents** Opening a Project File Detecting Simulation Instability Finding the Source of the Instability Fixing Deformation of the Garment Due to Sewing Lines Fixing Deformation of the Garment Due to Incorrect Layering of Patterns **[Download exercise file](http://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/E_Fixes/E-a_Simulation%20Instability%20A%20Portion%20of%20the%20Garment.zip) for Simulation Instability - A Portion of the Garment** **Opening a Project File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hQ-SzN3DG3Q \- This exercise will cover how to detect and resolve problems that may occur during Simulation. \- Open the file, Simulation Instability A Portion of the Garment, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to E_Fixes, then a_Simulation Instability A Portion of the Garment. Double click on the file, Simulation Instability A Portion of the Garment, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. **Detecting Simulation Instability** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5e5lmue_Hqg \- Turn on ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024355948/mceclip0.png)**Simulate**. Check for signs of unstable Simulation, usually indicated by layers poking through one another or portions of the 3D Garment shaking uncontrollably. **Finding the Source of the Instability** * **Strengthen the Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f-g2O7ZAMmo \- When the garment is tangled together, **Strengthen** all of the Patterns to flatten the garment. To Strengthen the Patterns, select all of them in the 2D Window with the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024271727/mceclip1.png) **Transform Pattern** Tool from the 2D Toolbar. Right click on one of them and select **Strengthen** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will appear orange in the 3D Window to indicate they have been Strengthened. \- When all of the Patterns have been flattened out it is easier to pinpoint the problem, such as an incorrectly sewn seam, on the 3D Garment. * **Simulate ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sgB9oy_dKfw \- Activate ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024355948/mceclip0.png) **Simulation**. **Fixing Deformation of the Garment Due to Sewing Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qt0mObFzfo4 \- Twisted or misplaced Sewing Lines are the most likely culprit of bunching and contorting of the 3D Garment. To learn how to remove them, reference the [Fixing Deformation of the Garment tutorial](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013410448). **Fixing Deformation of the Garment Due to Incorrect Layering of Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DkfUEZqKI1s \- Incorrectly layered Patterns are another cause of Simulation instability. **Unstrengthen** the Patterns and check the unstable parts of the garment. To Unstrengthen the Patterns, select all of them in the 2D Window with the**![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024271727/mceclip1.png) Transform Pattern** Tool from the 2D Toolbar. Right click on one of them and select **Unstrengthen** from the pop-up menu. The Patterns will no longer appear orange in the 3D Window. \- To learn how to fix this, reference the [Simulation Instability – Layered Patterns and Gizmo Tool tutorial](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013254447). title: How to Create Fur: Material Type "Fur (Render Only)"
content: #### **List of Contents** Apply Fur Fur Parameters Fur Gradation Color Fur Base Fur Maps (+ Fur Cluster Generator) Fur Gravity Fur Curl Fur Variance #### **Fur (Render Only) is a material type through which you can visualize realistic fur, fleece, etc. It can be applied onto any component in your 3D window or Object Browser that shows a Property Editor with a material type option. (E.g. fabrics, buttons, trims, avatars...) ** **This material type is render only, which means it can only be previewed during[Interactive Render](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). If you wish to preview fur in the 3D window, check out material type [Fur Strand](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44205065227801-Create-Fur-Strand-Beta).** **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/47286526797721)** #### #### **Apply Fur** 1. [Change the Material Type](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-Material-Type) to **fur (render only)**. 2. If desired, select one of the presets to express fox, mink, angora, sherpa and more. #### #### **Fur Parameters** ** Option ** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- **Melanin** | Higher melanin value tints the color browner and darker. The lower the value, the more similar the color remains to the original color you set before. **Pheomelanin** | Higher pheomelanin value tints the fur redder. This value functions proportionally to the melanin value; the pheomelanin value is not taken into account when the melanin value is 0. **Glossiness** | Configure shininess of the fur. When light is shone onto the fur, a higher value makes it shinier. **Glossiness Boost** | Express coated fur. Glossiness adjusts intrinsic shininess of the fur whereas Glossiness Boost expresses the shininess from the fur finishing, like wax or coating. The higher the Glossiness Boost value is, the stronger the fur finishing effect appears. **Softness** | Express smoothness of the fur. Higher Softness value is makes the fur smoother. A lower makes it rougher. **Compensate Energy** | If light cannot pass through denser hair sufficiently, this compensates for a lack of light bounces throughout the affected area. #### #### **Fur Gradation Color** Click the check box to change any gradation properties. **Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Fur Gradation Color ** | ** Color ** | Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. **Position** | Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. ** Interpolation ** | Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. #### #### **Fur Base** ** Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- ** Length ** | Configure the length of the fur. A higher value corresponds to longer fur. Example: Length = **50 vs. 10** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033587) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033607) ** Thickness ** | Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. A higher value corresponds to thicker strands. Example: Thickness = **10 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956288) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033607) **Bend** | Configure the bending strength of the fur. A higher value causes the strands to be more affected by gravity, therefore bending more. Example: Bend = **1 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033807) ![Untitled_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033787) **Taper** | Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. A higher value makes the strands become thinner towards their ends. A low value keeps a similar thickness between roots and ends. Example: Taper (with Thickness 2.00) = **1.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956388) ![Untitled_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956448) **Density** | Configure how closely placed the strands are. Higher value corresponds to denser fur. Lower value gives a more scattered appearance. Example: Density = **1 vs. 0.20** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033587) ![Untitled_6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956468) **Segments** | Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. When the fur is long and has a higher bending value, the fur must have a higher amount of segments to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for short and straight fur, this value is not as significant. #### #### **Fur Maps** Use base maps to express different levels of length, thickness, density, curl, bend, gravity, bend direction, and initial direction within a single pattern piece. **Maps for bend, length, thickness, density, curl, and gravity, like roughness and metalness maps, use a monochrome image as input** , with the image’s color values serving as the multiplier for the bend parameter. 0 is multiplied to the values when a map is black, while 1 is multiplied to the values when a map is white. **Maps for initial direction and bend direction define the direction of the fur and, like normal maps, use an RGB image as input** in red, green, and blue tones. The initial direction map determines the direction in which the fur initially grows, while the bend direction map defines how the fur curves from root to tip. _ Example: ![map_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360017402834) _ ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475777301017) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475800641817) You can easily generate the realistic Fur Cluster by controlling the length and bend direction. 1. 1. Open the **Fur Cluster Generator** by clicking the ![Inner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475777303833) button. 2. Generate the Fur Cluster. **Properties**** **| ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Length ** ** ** ** ** | ** Cropping Map ** **** | Use the Cropping Map to apply different length within a single pattern piece. **Mode** | As a cropping map is grayscale, the length is determined based on the level of darkness (RGB) or the transparency (Alpha). Transparent and black areas have the lowest Length, while opaque and white areas have the highest Length. **Level** | Adjust intensity of gray tones. Increasing the value makes the cropping effect more obvious. **Low/High Length** | Adjust the shortest or longest fur length. ** Trimming ** ** ** | **Intensity** | Trim the length from the edge to the center of the fur cluster. Higher intensity increases the difference in fur length from the edge to the center to create a sharper fur. #### ![Fur Cluster_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510720113945) **Random** | Higher randomization makes the clumps irregular, while lower randomization makes the clumps consistent. ![Fur Cluster_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40718701504025) ** Bend Direction ** **** | ** Cluster ** | **Intensity** | Adjusts the intensity of the fur bending in each direction. Higher intensity makes the fur clump more pronounced and dimensional. ![Fur Cluster_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510720146713) **Pores Density** | Adjust the pores density of the fur cluster. Higher density makes the clumps smaller and tighter, while lower density makes the clumps larger and more spread out. ![Fur Cluster_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40153821981977) **Direction/****Intensity Random** | Adjust whether the bend direction is consistent or irregular. ** Detail Cluster ** | The clumping of smaller sub-units within the cluster can be adjusted in the same way as the cluster. **Relax** | Adjust the intensity of clumping in detail clusters while keeping each direction intact. title: Project File (ZPRJ) Open/Add/Save
content: #### **List of Contents** **Open or Add** **Save** #### All information, including garments, avatars, 3D environments(background, lighting, wind, camera and simulation), animations, and so on, can be saved and loaded as one project file(ZPRJ). #### #### **Open or Add** 1. Click Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open/Add ▶ **Project.** _* Open the file directly by dragging it from the OS Explorer to the 3D window or by right-clicking the file in CLO Library and clicking**Add to Workspace**. _ __ 2. Navigate and select the Project file to be added and click **Open**. 3. Apply any detailed settings, then click on the **OK** button. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Load Type** | Open a new project file or add the file additionally. If you add additional files, you can set the position of the object in the X, Y, and Z axis. **Object** | Select the contents to load within the project file. (Items that are not included will be disabled.) [**Colorway**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/32783140814105-Colorway) | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48730788207001) Choose specific colorways you want to open or add by clicking the ![Select Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48732648870041) **Select Colorway.**[**![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/50834108001689)**](https://youtu.be/BxfRrxCtaXc?si=6Rb38Qvse-yv7d86)![Thumbnail=On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48732696469017) _* The thumbnail for each colorway shows the fabric that is most extensively used in that garment. However, the files created in 2025.1 or eariler will show only colorway names, without thumnails._ **📝Note:** When adding colorways, if you add more colorways than currently exist, the current colorway will be automatically duplicated to fill the gap. The items added this way (fabrics, graphics, trims, etc.) will be linked, so you can choose to unlink either only the materials or all properties. **Display Settings** | Select **Display Settings** to open the project file with the saved [3D and 2D display settings](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29838353719321-Display-Setting-ver-2024-0). **📝 Note:** * If Display Settings is not selected, the display settings are reset to default. * When loading a previous file ver 2024.2 or before, Display Settings is deactivated. Please resave it in the new version for activating Display Settings. #### #### **Save** 1. Click Main Menu ▶ Save/Save As ▶**Project / Project (with Other Files)** 2. Set the location and name to save and click the **Save** button. 3. When saving as a project & other files, select the files ([Texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002686508-3D-Garment-Surface-Textures-Save), [DXF](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000493067-2D-Pattern-DXF-Import-Export), [PDF](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004273427-2D-Pattern-AI-PDF-Import-Export)) to be saved together and click the**OK** button.

content: ## **New in 2025.1** **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48959141980825)** **List of Contents** Add Delete When Importing or Exporting 3D files, users can save their configured options as a preset for reuse.
